summaries.gardner: ZTO leads China's express-delivery industry by volume and is founder-led, but the industry is maturing, the stock has fallen about 21% since April 2026 and its edge is low cost rather than a breakthrough product. It fits Gardner's top-dog trait but misses the emerging-industry, momentum and 'overvalued' traits.
summaries.buffett: ZTO is simple to understand, profitable every year, conservatively financed (RMB31.3 billion of cash and short-term investments against RMB21.8 billion of debt at June 30, 2026) and trades near 10.7 times earnings. But its service is close to a commodity with weak pricing power, as the 2025 price war showed when gross margin fell from 31.0% to 25.0%, and returns on equity are in the mid-teens rather than exceptional.
summaries.munger: The cost-leadership flywheel (more parcels, denser routes, cheaper delivery) is a real advantage and management is rational about capital returns. Thinking backwards, the main ways it fails are a renewed price war, platform owners steering volume and the governance risks of a Chinese VIE structure, which keep it from being a 'great business at a fair price' in Munger's sense.
summaries.lynch: ZTO is a stalwart-turned-slow-grower in a business Lynch would like for its boringness: parcels, trucks and sorting hubs. Its P/E of about 10.7 is below expected 2026 EPS growth of about 16%, and the company is shrinking its share count with buybacks, though insiders are not buying in the open market.
summaries.fisher: ZTO keeps investing in automation (781 automated sorting sets, AI customer service handling over 70% of work orders) and new services such as retail and returns parcels, and its founder has run it since 2002. Fisher would question its weak pricing power, low margins in some years and limited disclosure on R&D results.
summaries.graham: ZTO passes several defensive tests: large size, profits in every recent year, EPS per ADS up from RMB5.42 in 2020 to RMB11.19 in 2025, a P/E around 11 on three-year average earnings and P/E times P/B of about 17. It fails the 20-year dividend record, having paid dividends only in recent years.
summaries.thiel: ZTO is not a monopoly: it holds about a fifth of China's parcel volume alongside YTO, STO, Yunda, J&T and SF, and its technology is better but not ten times better. It does have strong distribution through 6,000 network partners and 31,000 outlets, but fails most of Thiel's seven questions.
summaries.gerstner: Gerstner would value ZTO's efficiency, buybacks and cheap multiple (forward P/E about 9.9), but it does not ride a major platform shift like AI or cloud, and growth depends on a slowing Chinese consumer. It is a cash-generating value name rather than a compounding growth leader.
summaries.druckenmiller: Earnings re-accelerated in Q2 2026 (net income up 56.7%) as anti-involution price floors lifted core prices 15.5%, a possible catalyst, but the shares have fallen from about $25.6 in April to about $20, volume guidance was cut to 6-10% and J.P. Morgan downgraded it in September 2026. Liquidity and macro conditions in China are mixed, so conviction for a concentrated bet is low.
summaries.smith: ZTO has decent but not outstanding returns (2025 net margin 18.8%, ROE in the mid-teens), modest gross margins of about 25% and free cash flow of roughly 60% of net income after heavy capex. Terry Smith's preference for high-return, asset-light, resilient franchises makes it a weak fit despite the low price.
summaries.greenblatt: On the Magic Formula ZTO scores well on earnings yield: trailing operating income of about RMB11.4 billion against an enterprise value of roughly RMB93 billion is about 12%. Return on capital is moderate because the business owns hubs, land and trucks, so it ranks as cheap but only average quality.
summaries.akre: Akre's three legs are only partly met: management has a long record of execution and returns capital (target of at least 50% of prior-year adjusted net income), but the business's returns are moderate, pricing power is weak and reinvestment runway is shrinking as parcel growth slows.
summaries.pabrai: ZTO resembles a Dhandho bet in being simple, cheap and conservatively financed, with a temporary setback (the 2025 price war) that policy is helping to fix. The downside is cushioned by net cash and steady cash flow, but China and governance risks mean the chance of permanent loss is not negligible.
summaries.wood: ZTO is not an ARK-style disruptive innovator: it uses automation and AI to cut costs but is not a leader in AI, robotics, energy storage, blockchain or multiomics. Its addressable market is large but growing at single digits, not exponentially.
summaries.ackman: ZTO has some Ackman traits: a simple, predictable, cash-generative business, a dominant position in an industry with high barriers for new entrants, and a strong balance sheet. Weak pricing power, Chinese regulatory and VIE risk, and controlled governance work against it.
summaries.sleep: Nick Sleep would like ZTO's scale-economics-shared model, where falling unit costs (line-haul cost per parcel down 12.2% in 2025) let it charge less than rivals and win share. But the savings mostly went into a price war rather than a widening, customer-loved franchise, and its position in 10-20 years is not clearly stronger.
summaries.valentine: Valentine looked for huge, fast-growing markets and technology-driven companies early in their life; ZTO is a mature, 24-year-old operator in a large but slowing market. It solves a real problem for shippers but is not a venture-style opportunity.
summaries.nash: ZTO passes Nash's financial-strength checks (cash above debt, interest coverage over 40x, current ratio 1.7) and screens cheap on DCF and PEG, but it is a Chinese company (a zone to avoid), not part of a secular tech trend, and lags the S&P 500 over five years. Its Nash 13-category score is about 55, below the 75 bar.

momentum.evidence: The ADS fell from about $25.59 at the end of April 2026 to $20.17 on October 16, 2026 and is up only about 8% from $18.59 a year earlier, trailing the US market.

g4.evidence: Founder Meisong Lai has led ZTO since 2002 and Alibaba is a strategic shareholder, but the investor base is not a roster of famous growth investors.

g6.evidence: Analysts generally call it cheap, with a consensus Buy and an average target of $27.66, about 36% above the price, at a trailing P/E of about 10.7.

simple.evidence: ZTO collects a fee for moving parcels through its own hubs and trucks between partner-run outlets, an easy model to understand.

b2.evidence: Revenue rose every year from RMB25.2 billion in 2020 to RMB49.1 billion in 2025 and the company has been profitable throughout, with net income of RMB4.3 billion to RMB9.2 billion.

integrity.evidence: ZTO reports candidly and returns capital (a target of at least 50% of prior-year adjusted net income from 2026), but the founder controls voting through weighted voting rights and the group uses a VIE structure.

b6.evidence: ZTO mostly sticks to express delivery, but has made peripheral investments such as Cainiao Yizhan, on which it booked a RMB258.6 million impairment in Q4 2025.

roic.evidence: 2025 net income of RMB9.24 billion on about RMB65 billion of equity is a return of about 14% with low leverage, solid but not high for an asset-heavy network.

fcf.evidence: 2025 operating cash flow was RMB11.97 billion but capex of about RMB6.1 billion left free cash flow of roughly RMB5.9 billion, about 64% of net income.

b10.evidence: Equity grew to RMB63.7 billion, yet the ADS price fell from about $29 in October 2021 to about $20 in October 2026, so retained earnings have not lifted market value.

safety.evidence: A conservative DCF (about 11% growth, 13% FCF margin, 12% discount rate) gives roughly $22 per ADS, only about 10% above the $20.17 price.

fairprice.evidence: About 10.7 times trailing and 9.9 times forward earnings for a market leader growing revenue 22.5% in H1 2026 with net cash is a reasonable price.

mu5.evidence: Net cash and cost leadership make failure unlikely, but renewed price wars, platform-owned delivery and Chinese regulatory or delisting risks are real failure paths.

reinvest.evidence: ZTO reinvests about RMB6 billion a year in hubs and trucks at mid-teens returns, but slowing parcel growth limits how long it can do so.

ly2.evidence: It is a stalwart: the low-cost leader in Chinese parcels, growing with e-commerce and returning half its profits.

ly3.evidence: The trailing P/E of about 10.7 is below consensus 2026 EPS growth of about 16%.

runway.evidence: Retail parcels grew 46% in 2025 and ZTO is still gaining share (19.9% in Q2 2026), but industry growth is slowing toward single digits.

ly7.evidence: ZTO repurchased 31.8 million shares for $740 million in 2026 through Q2, but no open-market insider buying has been reported.

ly8.evidence: As a Chinese logistics stock it is under-owned in the US (institutions hold about 42%), though 17 analysts cover it.

fi2.evidence: Management is developing retail and reverse-logistics parcels, freight and international forwarding as core e-commerce delivery matures.

fi3.evidence: Technology spending shows results (missorting down about 60% with AI vision in 25 super sorting centers), but ZTO does not disclose R&D spending in detail.

fi4.evidence: ZTO wins key-account volume through price and coverage, gaining 0.8 points of share in Q4 2025, but this owes more to cost than to selling skill.

longterm.evidence: ZTO kept investing through the cycle, including RMB9.3 billion of capex in 2021 when free cash flow was negative, to build long-term cost leadership.

gr1.evidence: ZTO had RMB49.1 billion of 2025 revenue and a market value of about $15 billion.

ni10.evidence: ZTO has reported a profit every year since before its 2016 US IPO, including RMB4.3 billion to RMB9.2 billion each year from 2020 to 2025.

gr4.evidence: ZTO has paid dividends only in recent years, far short of a 20-year record.

eps10.evidence: Diluted EPS per ADS more than doubled from RMB5.42 in 2020 to RMB11.19 in 2025.

gr6.evidence: A market value of about RMB103 billion is about 11.5 times average 2023-2025 net income of about RMB9.0 billion.

gr7.evidence: A P/E of about 10.7 times a price-to-book of about 1.6 gives roughly 17, below 22.5.

th1.evidence: ZTO's automation gives it lower costs, but nothing like ten times better than YTO or J&T.

timing.evidence: Anti-involution price floors since 2025 are lifting prices (core ASP up 15.5% in Q2 2026), but parcel growth is slowing.

th3.evidence: ZTO grew up in a crowded, fast-growing mass market rather than dominating a small niche first.

team.evidence: Founder Meisong Lai has a 24-year record of building China's largest parcel network, but the team is strong operators rather than world-famous visionaries.

th5.evidence: ZTO reaches customers through over 6,000 direct network partners and over 31,000 pickup and delivery outlets.

durable.evidence: Parcel delivery will still be needed in 20 years and ZTO's scale is hard to copy, but platforms and automation could reshape who captures the profit.

dr2.evidence: If price floors hold, margins could recover toward 2024 levels, but slowing volume (6-10% growth guided for 2026) clouds the picture.

dr4.evidence: Lower Chinese interest rates and anti-involution policy help, but weak consumer demand and a 'subdued growth' environment hurt.

dr6.evidence: Catalysts include sustained price floors, $1.36 billion of remaining buyback capacity and continued share gains.

dr7.evidence: China risk, weak pricing power and slowing growth argue against a large concentrated position.

gm.evidence: Gross margin was 25.0% in 2025, down from 31.0% in 2024, reflecting a price-driven business.

pa4.evidence: Net cash, a low P/E and a 3.3% dividend yield limit downside, but Chinese regulatory and VIE risks remain.

wo3.evidence: ZTO does not combine several innovation platforms.
